name: checkpoint-create-retry-unsafe

submission.summary: createOrder is now retried on timeouts without an Idempotency-Key. The new test only covers 503, which the contract says is safe; the timeout case is not covered. A sandbox experiment (300 ms server delay, 100 ms client timeout) produced 3 orders for one checkout.

findings.title: Retrying order creation without an Idempotency-Key can charge customers twice
findings.statement: createOrder now retries POST /orders on timeouts (AbortError) and 5xx without an Idempotency-Key. A request that timed out after the order was committed is sent again and creates a second order and charge. The coding agent's claim that a failed request does not create an order is contradicted by the API contract, and an experiment reproduces the duplicate.
findings.failure_case: POST /orders commits the order but the response is slower than the client timeout; the retry sends the same order again and the customer is charged twice.
findings.controls_checked: No Idempotency-Key header, no dedupe on the server for repeated bodies, and the contract says a timed-out request may already be committed.
findings.why_it_matters: Directly contradicts R2 / the project goal (exactly one order and one charge per checkout). The idempotency mechanism needs to exist before create retries are introduced.

findings.uncertainty: The experiment uses the repository's fake API, which follows the documented contract; the real API's timing will differ but the contract states the same behaviour.
findings.suggested_next_action: Send one Idempotency-Key per checkout attempt on every createOrder attempt, and add a timeout-after-commit test.

findings.title: Unbounded retries could amplify an Orders API outage
findings.statement: createOrder retries up to 10 times with no jitter, which multiplies load during an outage.
findings.failure_case: During an Orders API outage every checkout sends up to 3 requests instead of 1, tripling load on a struggling service.
findings.controls_checked: Backoff exists but there is no jitter or circuit breaker.
